title: Market Analysis: Spinback Records & Coffee
subtitle: Demographic insights for Metro areas: Portland-South Portland, ME

summary.narrative:
Portland's 563,000-strong metro—young, educated, and culturally hungry—offers a prime stage for Spinback Records & Coffee to fuse vinyl nostalgia with third-wave coffee culture.

The Portland-South Portland, ME metropolitan area spans three geographic areas with a combined population of 563,380, forming a compact yet vibrant market well-suited to an experiential retail concept. Portland has cultivated a national reputation as a creative, food-and-drink-forward city, and that identity extends naturally to the kind of lifestyle destination Spinback aims to be. A hybrid model that pairs new and used vinyl, turntables, and specialty coffee with weekly listening parties and local artist showcases speaks directly to a community that already prizes independent culture, craft consumption, and communal gathering spaces.

The demographic landscape is defined by a concentration of the exact segments most likely to embrace vinyl and specialty coffee: culturally engaged young adults and millennials, higher-education-attaining professionals, and established creative-class residents with discretionary spending power. These groups drive the resurgence of vinyl as both a collectible and a lifestyle statement, and they treat specialty coffee shops as everyday "third places." With a manageable footprint of just three geographic areas covering more than half a million residents, Spinback can achieve meaningful market penetration without diluting its brand across a sprawling region.

Beyond raw demographics, the strategic advantage lies in Portland's density of foot traffic, tourism, and a proven appetite for locally-rooted retail experiences. The listening-party and artist-showcase programming positions Spinback not merely as a store, but as a recurring destination—converting one-time visitors into a loyal, repeat community that anchors both record sales and daily coffee revenue.
